hints.S12_A1: The dash lists the proof: RED FLOWERS, GOLDEN LANTERNS and laughter everywhere. Ask: does a GARDEN IN SPRING look empty, dark and quiet - or full of bright shades? Match the adjective to what your eyes would see.
hints.S12_A2: The FIREWORKS have just LIT UP THE NIGHT SKY and the children are full of JOY. Ask: which verb means to shout out loudly in excitement? 'Frowned' and 'slept' do not belong anywhere near joy.
hints.S12_A3: The MEAL is over and the TABLE must be made ready again for the ang pao. Ask: which phrasal verb means to tidy a mess away? 'Put off' delays, 'run away' escapes and 'give in' surrenders - none of them tidies anything.
hints.S12_A4: Everyone CHEERED AND CLAPPED because GOOD LUCK had arrived at the door. Ask: does this idiom mean ill, in trouble, or sad - or bursting with happiness? Idioms must be learnt whole; you cannot work them out word by word.
hints.S12_A5: Look at the little word FROM that follows the blank, and at the FASTING month. Ask: which verb is normally paired with 'from' to mean deliberately choosing not to do something? You resist a temptation, but never 'resist from' it.
hints.S12_B1: The subject is EVERYONE, not the whole FAMILY. Words like everyone and nobody behave like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb with -s?
hints.S12_B2: The word HAS is already in the sentence, waiting for a partner. Ask: which of the four forms can follow 'has' to build a present perfect - the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle?
hints.S12_B3: The GUESTS KNOCKED - one sudden moment that interrupted something already under way in the KITCHEN. Ask: which form shows an action in progress in the past? A plain past verb would only report a finished job.
hints.S12_B4: THIS YEAR is being measured against LAST YEAR - only two things compared. Ask: does a short adjective add -er, or take 'most'? And 'more' plus an -er ending is always wrong; never use both together.
hints.S12_B5: The second half explains WHY they STAYED UP PAST MIDNIGHT - they wanted to see the countdown. Ask: which joining word introduces a reason? 'So' would give the result instead, and 'although' would signal a contrast.
hints.S12_B6: The statement runs on IS ('The Chingay parade IS one of...'), and it is positive. Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag stay positive or flip to negative? The tag must reuse the same verb, not borrow 'does'.
hints.S12_B7: The blank comes straight before the noun GRANDPARENTS, so it must show who they belong to. Ask: can the subject pronoun 'you' ever describe a noun? A possessive form is needed - not the one that stands alone at the end of a sentence.
hints.S12_B8: The whole sentence looks back on a finished event: they went on FOR OVER AN HOUR and then took a REST. Ask: is the verb past or present here? It is a regular verb, so which ending does it take?
hints.S12_C1: The blank does the action of 'celebrated', and it stands for the writer together with BOTH sides of the family. Ask: does a subject take the acting form, or the receiving form? 'Us celebrated' can never be right.
hints.S12_C2: This blank does the action of 'brought', and it points back to MY UNCLE'S WIFE. Ask: does a subject take the acting form or the receiving form? 'Her brought a tray of MURUKKU' is not English.
hints.S12_C3: The blank sits right in front of the noun HUSBAND, so it must show who the husband belongs to - the uncle's wife. Ask: does a subject pronoun ever describe a noun? Only a possessive form can go before a noun.
hints.S12_C4: The writer says MY COUSINS AND I - so the parents in the KITCHEN belong to the whole group, the writer included. Ask: which possessive means 'belonging to me and the people with me'? Not one person alone, and not somebody else's.
hints.S12_C5: UNCLE carried out the final dish, and the blank is the one who PLACED it on the TABLE - a single man doing the action. Ask: does a subject take the acting form, or the owning form? 'His placed it' makes no sense.
hints.S12_C6: ALL THE CHILDREN were DELIGHTED, and the blank does the clapping and cheering - a whole group in action. Ask: does a subject take the acting form or the receiving form? 'Them clapped' is never right.
hints.S12_C7: The blank comes just before the noun MOTHER, and the crying cousin is a boy - 'comforted HIM' proves it. Ask: does a subject pronoun ever sit in front of a noun? Choose the possessive that belongs to one male.
hints.S12_C8: GRANDMOTHER entertained the whole group of CHILDREN with a SONG - so the group is receiving the action, not doing it. Ask: after a verb, does English use the subject form or the object form? 'Entertained they' is wrong.
hints.S12_D1: The clue is AFTER MONTHS OF BEING APART - the family has come back together at last. Ask: which box word describes people joined again after a separation? It follows 'we are', so it must be a describing word, not a noun like 'celebrations'.
hints.S12_D2: The house fills with MUSIC, LAUGHTER and the CHATTER of young and old. Ask: which box word means full of life, energy and activity? 'Celebrations' names an event, not the feel of a busy, noisy room.
hints.S12_D3: The example given is SWEEPING THE HOUSE before the new year to chase away BAD LUCK - one particular practice. Ask: which box word names such specific practices? Careful: the broader word for heritage handed down is wanted in blank 5.
hints.S12_D4: The proof follows the dash: they BRING FOOD, GIFTS AND RED PACKETS for everyone. Ask: which box word describes people who give freely? Watch the form - after 'are' an adverb ending in -ly cannot fit.
hints.S12_D5: The clue is PASSED DOWN FOR GENERATIONS and a deep sense of BELONGING - more than mere HABITS. Ask: which box word names long-established practices handed from grandparent to grandchild? The word for one specific practice is used in blank 3.
hints.S12_E1: The underlined word means 'at this place', but the sentence is about the SOUND of music reaching you from the flat. Ask: which spelling belongs to your ears? The two are said the same way, so choose by meaning.
hints.S12_E2: She had TWENTY NEIGHBOURS at her home, so the verb is right in meaning but wrong in spelling. Ask: in this word, does the -v- really come after the -i-? Say the base word slowly: in - vite.
hints.S12_E3: The family came in their BRIGHTEST CLOTHES - the verb itself is right, but a letter has gone missing. Ask: how many times does -r- appear in the base word? Keep every letter of the base word when you add the ending.
hints.S12_E4: The subject is THE CHILDREN - more than one. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular form of 'to be', or the plural one? Match the verb to the number of the subject, never to the word beside it.
hints.S12_E5: The SHOES belong to the guests - many people, not one. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? Decide where the apostrophe must sit when the owners are more than one.
hints.S12_F1: The TEACHER is reporting a yes/no question. Ask three things: which little linking word must follow ASKED? Does the reported question keep question word order, or normal statement order? And what happens to 'you' and to the present tense?
hints.S12_F2: GRANDMOTHER was in the middle of one action when the other suddenly happened. Ask: which of the two is the long background action, and which one cuts in? WHEN goes in front of the sudden event - and never drop the helping verb.
